title: ImPress: Securing DRAM Against Data-Disturbance Errors via Implicit Row-Press Mitigation
problem: DRAM cells suffer from Data-Disturbance Errors (DDE) including Rowhammer (from repeated row activation) and Row-Press (from keeping rows open), with Row-Press significantly reducing the activation count needed to induce errors and breaking existing Rowhammer mitigations.
motivation: Securing DRAM against DDE vulnerabilities is essential for system security as these errors can be exploited to compromise system integrity and confidentiality.
method: In-Press treats a row open for a specified time as equivalent to an activation using a Unified Charge-Loss Model that combines both Rowhammer and Row-Press effects. The solution is compatible with both controller-based trackers (Graphene, PARA) and in-DRAM trackers (Mithril, MINT), does not restrict row-open-time, and does not reduce the Rowhammer threshold.
key_novelty: Implicit row-open-time tracking through a unified charge-loss model that transparently extends existing Rowhammer mitigations to protect against Row-Press without performance overhead or threshold reduction.
contributions: Proposes Implicit Row-Press (In-Press) mitigation that treats row-open-time as equivalent to activation
Develops Unified Charge-Loss Model combining Rowhammer and Row-Press effects for arbitrary access patterns
Demonstrates compatibility with both controller-based (Graphene, PARA) and in-DRAM (Mithril, MINT) trackers
Shows transparent Row-Press resilience for existing Rowhammer solutions without performance degradation or threshold reduction

metrics.other: Transparent mitigation without affecting Rowhammer threshold or performance

limitations: Limitations not discussed in abstract; focused on DRAM Row-Press mitigation.
primary_theme: DRAM security via implicit row-press mitigation
